answer: Admission is a terrace, not a queue: each step up demands work the step below did not, and none can be skipped by paying twice — proof of unique runtime, then a task authored that epoch by a random established peer. Each tide of arrivals, the same-epoch registrants, is priced as one pool, so difficulty rises with the crowd and N puppets pay N full ladders, no bulk discount. Standing is an ember, not a balance: rekindled each epoch by work with strangers, it dims when counterparties recur. Attackers pay coordination and bond exposure per identity; honest agents climb once.
